pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome - The Bishop Wand Church Of England School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
As Headteacher, I am immensely proud to lead a community that consistently delivers academic excellence, outstanding pastoral care, and a vibrant co-curricular life.
At Bishop Wand, we are committed to nurturing the potential of every student, ensuring they leave us not only with exceptional qualifications but also as confident, compassionate and principled young adults ready to make a positive impact in the world.
Our students thrive in an environment that is ambitious, inclusive and values-driven. We set high expectations and provide the support and inspiration needed for every child to exceed them. Our dedicated staff are passionate about teaching and learning, and they work tirelessly to ignite curiosity, foster creativity and instil a lifelong love of learning.
Rooted in Christian values, our School ethos is built on kindness, respect and integrity. These values underpin everything we do and shape the character of our students. We are proud of our strong links with the Church of England and the Diocese of London, and we welcome families of all faiths and none, who share our commitment to excellence and community.
Our broad and balanced curriculum is enriched by a wealth of opportunities beyond the classroom. Whether through our award-winning performing arts, competitive sports, leadership programmes or community outreach, students are encouraged to explore their interests and develop their talents. We believe that a truly outstanding education develops the whole child.
We also recognise the vital role that parents and carers play in a child’s success. At Bishop Wand, we value strong partnerships with families and are committed to working together to support your child’s academic progress and personal development.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bishop Wand ACE Programme in partnership with Harlequins - The Bishop Wand Church Of England School
pageCache.text:
Bishop Wand ACE Programme in partnership with Harlequins
Admissions Information
There will be 25 places available in Year 12 and Year 13 for students studying in the Sixth Form alongside the programme. If you require any additional information, please contact Mr Slatem our ACE Head Coach lslatem@bishopwand.surrey.sch.uk
What is the Programme?
The ACE scheme – Academy, Colleges and Education - is targeted at talented Year 12 and Year 13 students who have the aspirations and potential to play elite rugby. The ACE scheme gives boys the opportunity to combine rugby training with education here at The Bishop Wand Church of England School. This combination allows the students to not only gain an excellent education but also experience high-quality rugby training and match opportunities.
The rugby component of the combined development process will be delivered at the training ground at Hazelwood in Sunbury and will be led by ACE Head Coach Liam Slatem lslatem@bishopwand.surrey.sch.uk alongside Ben Goldie from Harlequins F.C. We also have a Strength and Conditioning Coach and a Physiotherapist that work with the ACE students as part of the programme.
Academic Requirements
The minimum entry requirement to study at The Bishop Wand Sixth Form is five GCSE passes at grade 4 or above. Please note that the specific entry requirements for many of our subjects is grade 5 or higher at GCSE and many courses require English and Maths at a good level too. Please refer to our course booklet or online prospectus for the entry requirements for each course.
Bishop Wand ACE Rugby Programme
Application & Recruitment – At a Glance
Talented rugby players entering Sixth Form who want to combine education at Bishop Wand with elite rugby development through the Harlequins pathway.
Application Timeline:
• Sep 2026: Programme information released via Bishop Wand & Harlequins. ACE applications open.
• Oct 2026: Bishop Wand Open Evening (Thursday, 15th October). ACE rugby presentation & Q&A
• Dec 2026: ACE Trial 1
• Jan 2027: ACE Trial 2 (invite only)
• Feb 2027: Final ACE Trial (invite only)
• Apply for the ACE Rugby Programme. Sign up for the ACE trials by using the QR code.
Trial sign up QR code: (Available from 15th October 2026)
• Attend trials if invited
• Apply separately to Bishop Wand Sixth Form (required for all students)
Bishop Wand Sixth Form Application: (Available from 15th October 2026)
*Important: Applying for ACE does not guarantee a Bishop Wand Sixth Form place. You can still apply to Bishop Wand even if you are not selected for ACE.
*If you are interested in being considered for a place at Bishop Wand Sixth Form, even if you are unsuccessful with applying for the ACE programme, please ensure you complete the application form by the deadline date Friday, 18th December 2026.

pageCache.pageTitle: Careers and Work Experience - The Bishop Wand Church Of England School
pageCache.text:
Careers and Work Experience
At the Bishop Wand Church of England School, we strive to ensure that all students are prepared, regardless of their background, for further and higher education and employment. This applies to students seeking Post-16 and Post-18 future employment, education or training placements.
Information and guidance are incorporated into the Citizenship Programme that is taught throughout the School to all students. An adviser from Innervate Careers Service is also available to meet with students to discuss their personal interest and plans and a ‘drop in' session is available during the lunchtime on a weekly basis.
In Year 10 students have the Work Experience Programme, which includes a compulsory Mock Job Interview and Feedback Event, which helps prepare young people for their first steps in the world of work. The Programme also includes the opportunity for Year 10 and Year 12 students to undertake a minimum of one week’s work experience, during the summer term.
Career talks with outside speakers from a wide range of industries and organisations are also arranged for students to attend.
Trips to career fairs, universities and individual businesses and organisations are arranged for students across all key stages, to further enhance their awareness of future career paths.
Email: admin@bishopwand.surrey.sch.uk
https://nationalcareers.service.gov.uk/ – This is the Government’s hub for careers advice for people of all ages where you can find help with drafting letters, CVs, exploring your skills or seeking careers advice.
https://www.gov.uk/topic/further-education-skills/apprenticeships – the National Apprenticeship Service website provides general advice and information about apprenticeships. Also advertises current vacancies.
www.icould.com – aims to help you to make the most of your potential by showing how others have used theirs, take the ‘Buzz’ personality profile quiz.
www.startprofile.com – investigate careers, watch videos and get great advice, find out about employers and work experience opportunities in your area.
www.careersbox.co.uk – video-based job profile information and skills explorer tool.
www.successatschool.org – gives clear and comprehensive information about a range of Career Zones (sectors), in an easy to access format. Students can create a profile to help to collate useful information. ’60 second interviews’ giving profile of professionals, provide a useful insight into specific careers.
www.how2become.com – offers detailed advice on how to access a range of sectors. Also offers the purchase of resources, compiled in conjunction with professionals working in these fields, designed to enable you to achieve your dream career or course. A selection of these books and online psychometric testing access have been supplied to the School by How2Become.
www.notgoingtouni.co.uk– opportunities that exist outside of university.
www.ucas.com – information about university courses on offer, also the Stamford test to help with ideas about subjects to study.
www.russellgroup.ac.uk – represents 24 leading universities, source of careers information & advice including ‘informed choices’ a downloadable guide to making post 16 choices.
www.springpod.co.uk - virtual work experience programmes
apply.army.mod.uk - Operator Technical Intelligence
apply.army.mod.uk - Business and Human Resources
educationprojects.co.uk - Ward Round Live. Virtual hospital work experience course for students aged 15+

pageCache.pageTitle: Admissions Appeals - The Bishop Wand Church Of England School
pageCache.text:
Admissions Appeals
Appeals for September 2026 resulting from year of entry or transfer applications:
Appeals to be heard by
16 June 2026 (40 School days)
Please note: Appeals will not start being heard until after the closing date has passed.
Appeals lodged after these dates will be heard within 40 school days of the appeal deadline or 30 school days of being lodged, whichever is the later date.
Appeals are not heard in the holidays.
Appellants will be sent notification of their appeal hearing at least 10 clear school days in advance of the hearing. Appellants will be sent a copy of the school's case normally a week in advance of the hearing.
Appellants must ensure that any further evidence not included with their initial appeal, is received by the stated deadline, which will be clearly highlighted in the appeal hearing notification letter. Any additional evidence or information received after this date might not be considered at the appeal hearing.
In year or immediate entry appeals
Appeals resulting from in year admission applications will be heard within 30 school days of the appeal being lodged.
Further details on how to lodge an appeal can be found here https://www9.surreycc.gov.uk/SchoolsDirectory/
